mainTopic: Ruling on the נדרי זירוזין dispute, then the משנה on נדרי הבאי and the search for a case of שבועות הבאי
overview: This amud opens by finishing an argument from the previous amud. The גמרא concludes that the רבנן really disagree with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב about נדרי זירוזין, then asks whose view is the הלכה. רב הונא and רב אדא בר אהבה both rule like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. Next comes a new משנה with examples of נדרי הבאי, vows tied to obvious exaggerations, like seeing a crowd as big as those who left מצרים. A ברייתא adds that נדרי הבאי are not binding, but שבועות הבאי are binding. The גמרא then searches for the exact case of such an oath. אביי suggests 'I swear that I saw,' but רבא rejects this and gives his own case: 'all the produce of the world is forbidden to me by oath if I did not see' that crowd. רבינא then asks רב אשי whether the man might have truthfully meant an anthill, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier argument and concludes that the רבנן really do disagree with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: [It must mean] that even in the earlier cases [they disagree], and so we learn that the רבנן disagree with him. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing a sentence from the previous discussion. It reaches a conclusion: the רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion asked whether רבי אליעזר בן יעקב was only adding to the רבנן or arguing with them. The words 'even in the earlier cases' mean that the רבנן disagree even about the first cases of נדרי זירוזין, where he was not irritated, and hold that those vows are binding. So there is a real מחלוקת, and the גמרא confirms it with 'שמע מינה'.

keyTerms.meaning: the earlier ones, meaning the first cases discussed
learn from it; a formula that confirms a conclusion
they disagree
the Sages (the majority opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: This step starts in the middle of a sentence that began in the previous section. Don't look for a new opening here; it is the end of an argument already in progress.

phrases.english: that even in the earlier ones,
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence before it; 'the earlier ones' are the first cases, about נדרי זירוזין.

phrases.english: and learn from it that the Rabbis disagree with him.
Learn from it [indeed].

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the argument from the previous section of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The רבנן and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב are in a real disagreement.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: Now that there is a real מחלוקת, the גמרא asks which opinion the הלכה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion on this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical ruling. It is setting up the next step, where the answer will come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 showed that the two sides really argue. So the next question is obvious: whose view do we follow? This is a plain request for the הלכה, not a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: what came of it? (what is the ruling on this?)

phrases.english: What was [concluded] about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical ruling on the מחלוקת confirmed in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה follows the רבנן or רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: Two אמוראים rule like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב אדא בר אהבה both rule that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב הונא said the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. And רב אדא בר אהבה also said the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 2. Two אמוראים each rule like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though he argues with the רבנן, the הלכה goes like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. Bringing a second אמורא who says the same thing ('וכן אמר') makes the ruling stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear; introduces a source that answers a question
the הלכה follows...
and so said; another authority agrees

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, as both רב הונא and רב אדא בר אהבה rule.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav Huna said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: and so said Rav Adda bar Ahava:
The halakha is like Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical ruling for the whole discussion about נדרי זירוזין.

steps.title: משנה: examples of exaggerated vows
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives examples of נדרי הבאי, vows built on obvious exaggeration.
steps.simpleTranslation: Vows of exaggeration: a person said, 'קונם [this item to me] if I did not see on this road as many people as those who left מצרים,' or 'if I did not see a snake as big as the beam of an olive press.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains what נדרי הבאי are by giving two examples of wild exaggeration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both examples, the person ties a vow to a claim that is clearly overstated: a huge crowd, or an enormous snake. Everyone understands he is just talking big, not really making a vow. That is why these belong on the list of vows that are not binding.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה
vows of exaggeration (empty talk)
a vow word meaning 'forbidden to me like a קרבן'
those who went up out of Egypt (the huge nation at יציאת מצרים)
the giant beam used to press olives

phrases.english: MISHNA: Vows of exaggeration [are, for example, when]
he said: 'Konam if I did not see
on this road [as many] as those who went up from Egypt,'
'if I did not see a snake
like the beam of an olive press.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a new משנה about נדרי הבאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vows tied to obvious exaggerations count as נדרי הבאי and are not binding.

steps.title: Exaggerated vows are permitted, exaggerated oaths are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that נדרי הבאי are not binding, but שבועות הבאי are binding.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: vows of exaggeration are permitted; oaths of exaggeration are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that adds a new rule. Exaggeration cancels a נדר, but it does not cancel a שבועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה spoke only about נדרים. The ברייתא adds that a שבועה is different: even a שבועה linked to an exaggerated claim stays binding. So the leniency of הבאי applies only to נדרים.

keyTerms.meaning: the discussion on the משנה
a Sage taught (introduces a ברייתא)
permitted (the vow does not take effect)
oaths
forbidden (the oath takes effect)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume a שבועה works the same way as a נדר here. The exact same exaggeration that cancels a נדר does not cancel a שבועה.

phrases.english: GEMARA: A Sage taught:
Vows of exaggeration are permitted,
phrases.notes: Permitted means the item he tried to forbid stays permitted, because the vow never took hold.

phrases.english: oaths of exaggeration are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that sets a limit on the משנה's rule: it applies to נדרים, not to שבועות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נדרי הבאי are not binding, while שבועות הבאי are binding.
steps.whyThisMatters: It draws a key line between נדרים and שבועות, showing that a שבועה is treated more seriously.

steps.title: What does an exaggerated oath look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact case of a שבועת הבאי mentioned in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of oaths of exaggeration?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of case the ברייתא means by שבועות הבאי. This question sets up the attempts that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said שבועות הבאי are binding but did not describe one. The גמרא wants a concrete wording, so it can see how such an oath could be binding while the matching נדר is not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?
Oaths built on obvious exaggeration

phrases.english: What is the case of oaths of exaggeration?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the concrete case behind the ברייתא's rule in Step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording and case of a שבועת הבאי.

steps.title: The first suggestion is not even a real oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the oath matches the נדר's wording, then rejects it because that wording says nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is someone who said, "An oath, if I did not see on this road [as many people as left מצרים]," is he saying anything?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the simplest idea, copying the wording of the נדר הבאי but using the word "oath," and then rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "An oath, if I did not see…" is an unfinished sentence. It does not say what he is swearing to or what becomes forbidden, so it is not a real שבועה at all, even if he meant it seriously.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, a first suggestion that will be rejected
Is he saying anything? (No, his words mean nothing.)

phrases.english: If you say it is where he said:
"An oath, if I did not see
on this road"
phrases.notes: The full exaggeration from the משנה is understood here: "as many people as those who left מצרים."

phrases.english: Is he saying anything?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects a first answer to the question in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested wording of the שבועת הבאי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The sentence has no content, so it is not a valid oath at all.

steps.title: אביי: he swore that he saw
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the case is one who swears that he did see that many people.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is where he said, "An oath that I saw [as many people as left מצרים on this road]."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers with a wording that is a complete oath: "I swear that I saw."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the rejected wording, "I swear that I saw" is a full statement about the past. If it is false, he has made a false oath, so it is binding.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, often in debate with רבא
That I saw

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Where he said, "An oath that I saw."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a valid oath wording after Step 7 rejected the first one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שבועת הבאי is "I swear that I saw" that huge crowd.

steps.title: רבא: that is obvious, and it doesn't match the נדר
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי with two problems: his case teaches nothing new, and it does not parallel the נדר's wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If so, why do I need it said? And also, the ברייתא teaches the oath as similar to the vow!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's answer from two sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, a false "I swear that I saw" is plainly a false oath, so the ברייתא would not need to teach it. Second, the ברייתא sets the oath side by side with the נדר, and the נדר said "if I did not see," so the oath should use the same form.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it said? (It is obvious.)
And furthermore, a second objection
Similar to, parallel with

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
If so, why do I need to say it?
And furthermore: it teaches it similar to a vow!
phrases.notes: The vow said "if I did not see," so the matching oath should also be about not seeing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אִם כֵּן לְמָה לִי לְמֵימַר
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's case of "I swear that I saw."
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It teaches nothing new, and it breaks the parallel with the נדר, which used "if I did not see."

steps.title: רבא: all produce forbidden by oath if I didn't see
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives his own case: a full oath, built like the נדר, forbidding all produce if he did not see that crowd.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It is where he says, "Let all the produce of the world be forbidden to me by an oath if I did not see on this road as many as those who left מצרים."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces אביי's case with one that answers both of his own objections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This wording is a complete oath, because it states what becomes forbidden. It also uses "if I did not see," just like the נדר. So the ברייתא teaches something new: the same wording does not work as a נדר, yet it is binding as a שבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, rejecting the earlier answer and giving a new one
Let them be forbidden
Those who left מצרים, a huge crowd

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, a שבועת הבאי is a full oath built like the נדר: "all produce is forbidden to me by oath if I did not see as many as left מצרים."

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: where he says:
"Let the produce of the world be forbidden to me by an oath
if I did not see on this road
as many as those who left Egypt."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the two objections of Step 9 with a new case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שבועת הבאי is "I swear that I saw" (אביי).
steps.terutzMaskana: It is an oath forbidding all produce if he did not see the crowd, worded just like the נדר.

steps.title: רבינא: maybe he saw an anthill
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי whether the man might not be exaggerating at all, but really saw a huge number of ants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But perhaps this man saw an anthill and called the ants "those who left מצרים," and he swore truthfully?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רבא's case: maybe it is not an exaggeration at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the man meant an anthill, then his oath could be true. Then why call it a שבועת הבאי? The answer will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
An anthill, a nest of ants
He swore properly, truthfully

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
But perhaps this man
saw an anthill
and gave them the name "those who left Egypt,"
and he swore properly?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: וְדִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבא's case in Step 10 is really an exaggeration.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's case of the oath about seeing "those who left מצרים."
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he meant a crowd of ants, the oath could be literally true, so it would not be an exaggerated oath at all.
